source: 1968 Chevrolet Chassis Service Manual, Steering, p.9-10

procedures.title: Steering column (energy absorbing): inspect for collision damage
steps: Inspect whenever damage shows, after any front-end collision, or whenever force has been applied to the wheel or column; replace any damaged parts.
Support bracket: look for mounting capsules separated from the bracket and the bracket moved forward toward the engine, which usually also collapses the mesh section.
Column: look for bulges or bends in the mesh section of the jacket.
Shifter shaft (where fitted): hold the lower end and move the column shift lever through its ranges and up and down; little or no shaft movement means the plastic joints have sheared.
Steering shaft: hold the shaft at the coupling and rock the wheel; any lash means the plastic pins have sheared.
If only the shaft pins sheared in a minor collision with no other damage, the car can still be steered safely, but replace the steering shaft.
notes: Caution: the mast jacket, shift tube, steering shaft and instrument panel mounting bracket are energy-absorbing parts; never hammer, jar, drop or lean on the column.

Telescopic (Corvette) column: the wheel, horn parts, turn signal switch, upper housing and bearing and related upper-end parts can be serviced with the column left in the car; skip removal and go to the disassembly steps.

procedures.title: Steering column: remove
parts: neutral safety and back-up lamp switch connectors
steps: Unplug the column harness, and the neutral safety and back-up lamp switch connectors if fitted.
Remove the steering wheel as described in this section.
Remove the nuts and washers holding the column's flanged end to the steering gear.
Disconnect any transmission linkage from the lower column shift levers.
notes: Mast jacket cover and dash panel trim steps for Chevrolet and Chevelle are omitted.
The manual's step 7 (remove screws joining the upper and lower covers and take the covers off) carries no model label.
